strategies.name: MACD Oscillator backtest.py
strategies.what_it_does: Despite the name, there is no MACD here: no 12/26 EMA, no signal line, no histogram. The script compares two simple moving averages of Close, with windows typed in at runtime (l.25-26, l.119-120; the comment at l.111 suggests 10 and 21). Position is 1 when SMA(ma1) >= SMA(ma2), otherwise 0, from bar ma1 onward (l.47). So it is long/flat, although README l.96 says 'Vice versa', i.e. a short. Trade markers are diff(positions) (l.51), drawn at that bar's Close (l.71-72), and the exit is labelled 'SHORT'. There is no sizing, no PnL and no stats, only plots (l.64-100); l.138-139 points to the Heikin-Ashi file for stats. Ticker and dates are user input through fix_yahoo_finance (l.121-131). The README preview (preview/macd positions.png) shows Boeing (BA) from about Oct 2012 to Jan 2013, with three markers and no equity curve.
strategies.code_flaws: (1) It is not a backtest at all: no returns, no costs (README l.19: 'all trades are frictionless. No slippage, no surcharge, no illiquidity'), no out-of-sample period, and one ticker chosen by the user. (2) The signal uses Close[t] and the trade is marked at Close[t], with no lag. (3) Warm-up bug: min_periods=1 (l.25-26) and positions start at index ma1 (l.47), so between bars ma1 and ma2 the 'long' average covers fewer bars than declared. (4) It uses chained assignment, signals['positions'][ma1:]=... (l.47). I re-typed that line on pandas 3.0.5 (my code, not theirs): the column is not modified and pandas raises a ChainedAssignmentError warning (check_output.txt, test A). On current pandas the script therefore plots zero trades. (5) It depends on the deprecated fix_yahoo_finance package (l.15). (6) Window lengths are typed by hand on every run, which invites cherry-picking.
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: Tested, as the same family. resource/08 l.120: Levine-Pedersen show that time-series momentum and moving-average crossovers are the same linear filters. SIG-3a, Carver's EWMAC binary on pairs (16,64), (32,128), (64,256), FAILED: B POST d -0.105 / w -0.074, with gross exposure up 36-42 % (resource/08 l.215; spec in 2026-10-22-trend-improvement-evidence/phase1_plan.md l.154; verdicts.md l.129-141). SIG-3b, EWMAC continuous, FAILED: C FULL d -0.619 (resource/08 l.216). SIG-6, the Baz MACD trio, was not pursued because its own evidence is 1.11 against 1.39 for the sign rule on zero-cost futures (resource/08 l.83, l.122; phase1_plan.md l.380; verify_signal.md l.205-215, which notes that the faster direction is worse). The faster lookback set (10,30,60) scored Sharpe 1.08 against 1.12 (2026-10-13-prop-strategy-evidence/backtest_results.md l.237). All 18 settings are in 2026-10-08-trend-following-backtest.md l.37. Rejected-table rows: resource/07 l.197-198. On the market-making side, a MACD shift of the reference price (Hummingbot PMM Dynamic) is recorded in resource/02 l.115 and resource/04 l.57. STRATEGY.md l.104-114 uses OFI and the Binance lead as the short-horizon alpha instead.
strategies.fits_delta: It could run on Delta daily closes for the nine coins, with taker market orders like the trend paper books, not through the post-only MM bot. Costs are not what kills it: a daily crossover that flips a few times a year per coin pays 14.62 bps per round trip, which is small. What kills it is that it is a cruder, non-vol-scaled member of the linear-filter family we already run. Our EWMA and faster variants tested worse on the 24 ex-ante perps and on Delta.
strategies.reason: Same family as SIG-3a, SIG-3b, SIG-6 and the T3d fast lookbacks, all of which failed or were dropped on evidence. The repo's version adds nothing: it has no PnL code, assumes no costs, has a warm-up bug, and does nothing on pandas 3.

strategies.name: Awesome Oscillator backtest.py
strategies.what_it_does: Two books on one ticker typed in at runtime (l.307-310). (1) 'MACD': EWMA span 5 against span 34 of Close (l.36-37, l.303-304), long when fast >= slow, otherwise flat (l.45). (2) 'Awesome': SMA5 and SMA34 of the median price (H+L)/2 (l.59-60), then a 'saucer' pattern block (l.84-102), then an MA-crossover block with a cumsum gate that allows one long at a time (l.113-123). Sizing is a fixed 100 shares on $5,000 starting cash (l.214-215), filled at the signal bar's Close (l.221-227). Its 'sharpe' is total return divided by the std of daily returns (l.285-286), plus a max-drawdown function (l.268-275). preview/awesome asset.png has no ticker label. Read off the chart, equity goes from 5,000 to about 20,500 (MACD) and about 17,800 (AO) between about Feb 2016 and Dec 2017. Comment l.326-331: MACD had the higher Sharpe, AO the smaller drawdown.
strategies.code_flaws: (1) The saucer block is dead code. Every saucer needs AO[i] of the same sign that makes the MA block overwrite that bar. I re-typed the loop and ran it on 30,000 synthetic bars: the saucer fired 2,108 times and changed the output on 0 bars, and the 'Awesome' output matched a plain SMA5/SMA34(HL2) long/flat crossover on every bar (check_output.txt, test B). So the README claim (l.150) that the saucer 'beats the slow response' is never exercised. The whole comparison is SMA(HL2) against EMA(Close) at 5/34. (2) Even if it were live, the saucer is wrong. It takes bar colour from candle Open/Close (l.84-86) rather than from the bar-to-bar change in AO. Its signs are inverted against the TradingView definition it cites (l.4): the block commented as 'Bearish Saucer' sets +1 (l.79-90) and the 'bullish' block sets -1 (l.93-102). Comment l.82 also has green and red backwards. (3) Fills at the same close: HL2 for bar t needs bar t's high and low, and the fill is bar t's Close (l.226-227). (4) No costs (README l.19). The fixed 100 shares ignore both price and the $5,000 cash, so leverage is unbounded and uncontrolled. (5) The 'Sharpe' mixes a whole-period return with a daily std and is not annualised (l.285). (6) One unnamed ticker, in-sample only. Chained assignment at l.45 does nothing on pandas 3 (test A). The loop recomputes the full cumsum on every bar (l.115, l.121), which is O(n^2).
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: It is a moving-average crossover, so the MACD evidence applies: resource/08 l.120 (equivalence), l.215-216 (SIG-3a and SIG-3b FAILED), l.83 (SIG-6 dropped). On speed: 5/34 days is faster than our fastest tested set, and (10,30,60) scored 1.08 against 1.12 (backtest_results.md l.237). verify_signal.md l.205-207 says the faster direction is worse. crypto_academic.md l.175 (secondary source) says Zarattini's 5-day BTC lookback 'collapses at 50 bps'. Rejected-table row: resource/07 l.198.
strategies.fits_delta: HL2 needs highs and lows, but the repo's Delta daily loader has O = H = L = C (resource/08 l.95), so it would need another loader. A 5/34 crossover flips often on 24/7 crypto daily bars. At 14.62 bps per round trip the costs are bearable, but that speed is the direction our tests found worse. The post-only MM bot has no use for it.
strategies.reason: In practice it is an SMA5/SMA34 crossover on the median price, because the saucer never changes a trade. That is a faster member of the linear-filter family that SIG-3a, SIG-3b, SIG-6 and T3d already covered and rejected.

strategies.name: Heikin-Ashi backtest.py
strategies.what_it_does: Builds Heikin-Ashi candles: close = (O+H+L+C)/4, open = (previous HA open + previous HA close)/2, high and low = max and min of HA open, HA close, High and Low (l.48-61). Entry (l.94-96): the current HA candle is bearish (HA open > HA close) with no upper wick (HA open == HA high), its body is larger than the previous body, and the previous candle was also bearish. Then it buys 100 shares, adding up to stls = 3 longs (l.103, l.405). Exit (l.107-121): the current HA candle is bullish with no lower wick and the previous one was bullish; then it sells everything. In effect it buys into an accelerating fall and sells after two up candles, which is a short-horizon dip-buy, although README l.118-120 calls Heikin-Ashi a momentum filter. Sizing is 100 shares on $10,000 cash (l.223). Stats: CAGR, Sharpe against the S&P 500, MDD, Calmar, omega, sortino (l.329-392). The demo is NVDA, 2015-04-01 to 2018-02-15 (l.406-408). preview/heikin-ashi asset value.png covers only about 2018-01-09 to 2018-02-14: two longs, and an end equity of about 13,500 read off the chart.
strategies.code_flaws: (1) The portfolio and all stats run on the plotting slice: viz = trading_signals[slicer:] with slicer = 700 (l.412, l.419-422). 2015-04-01 to 2018-02-15 has 751 weekdays (np.busday_count; NYSE sessions are fewer), so at most 51 bars are evaluated. Positions opened before the slice are dropped, and an exit inside it can push cumsum negative, which is an unintended short. The preview's Jan-Feb 2018 x-axis confirms this. (2) The stats are mismatched: growth rate and std are divided by len(trading_signals), the full sample, while the returns come from the slice (l.339-342). Sharpe and Calmar are per day, not annualised, and Calmar divides by a negative MDD (l.370). (3) omega() and sortino() integrate a standard Student-t whose degrees of freedom equal the sample length, so it is close to a normal with scale 1, between bounds set by daily returns of scale about 0.01 (l.280-301, l.371-372). They do not measure the strategy's return distribution. (4) It fills at Close[t] on a signal that uses bar t's OHLC. No costs (README l.19). 100 shares times up to 3 entries regardless of cash, so leverage is unbounded. (5) One stock, one in-sample window, stls set by hand. The HA open seed uses chained assignment (l.52), which does nothing on pandas 3. (6) The rules cite a Quantiacs blog I could not open, so I have not checked whether the bearish-candle entry matches the source.
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: Not tested by name: there is no hit for Heikin-Ashi or candlestick patterns in resource/, STRATEGY.md or the research memos. The closest evidence points against it. (a) Short-horizon direction ideas were rejected: 52.9-54.1 % daily directional accuracy, and naive sign strategies fail at 10 bps (resource/07 l.175). (b) Fading the previous-week level is the worst trade tested: -42.5 / -25.7 / -51.4 bps net at 4 h (cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-22-prev-week-levels.md l.25, l.41; resource/07 l.205). (c) For large liquid coins the 1-2 week horizon is momentum, not reversal (2026-10-22-trend-improvement-evidence/phase1/notes/crypto_academic.md l.52-53, Ficura-Colak t = 4.93, unverified secondary). (d) OVL-3: while the rule is long, the 'weak 20-day return' state still earned +0.61 % (2020-26) and +0.09 % (2022-26) over the next 7 days on the 24 ex-ante perps (resource/07 l.201). Short-term weakness in our universe kept paying rather than reversing.
strategies.fits_delta: It could run on daily OHLC, but the repo's Delta loader is close-only (resource/08 l.95), so it would need a candle loader. It is a counter-trend dip-buy on large caps, the direction our evidence argues against. As a long-only short-horizon rule it would be taker-executed at 14.62 bps per round trip, and the post-only MM bot cannot use it.
strategies.reason: The named rule is untested in our repo, but it has no evidence of edge. Its only result is about 50 bars of NVDA, measured with broken stats, and the closest evidence we have (short-horizon direction, level fades, large-cap 1-2 week momentum, the OVL-3 diagnostic) points the other way. It does not reach the bar for a screen.

strategies.name: Parabolic SAR backtest.py
strategies.what_it_does: Wilder's Parabolic SAR with acceleration factor starting at 0.02, step 0.02, max 0.2 (l.34-36), computed recursively (l.53-81). Position is 1 when SAR < Close, otherwise 0 (l.98): long/flat, with trades marked at the bar's Close (l.99, l.119-120) and the exit labelled 'SHORT'. No sizing, no PnL and no stats; l.162-163 points to the Heikin-Ashi file. The demo is Electronic Arts (EA), 2016-01-01 to 2018-01-01 (l.134-136), with the plot sliced from bar 450 (l.140). The preview covers about mid-Oct to end-Dec 2017 and shows four markers.
strategies.code_flaws: (1) The recursion is wrong. After a reversal the script stores Wilder's reset value, the prior extreme point (EP), in 'real sar' (l.72-74, l.81). But the next bar's SAR is built from 'sar' (l.55), which still holds the old trend's value, and is then clamped to the last two lows or highs. I compared a re-typed copy with a textbook Wilder SAR on 40,000 synthetic bars at 3.5 % daily vol. The script reversed 5,437 times against Wilder's 4,025, its long/flat position differed on 11.0 % of bars, and the day after a reversal its median SAR distance from Close was 7.86 % against 11.04 % (check_output.txt, test C). The script's stop is tighter than Wilder's and whipsaws more. (2) The initial SAR in an uptrend is set to High[0], above price (l.47). This is inverted, but the clamp at bar 2 washes it out. (3) Same-bar: the reversal test uses bar t's High and Low and the position flips at Close[t]. A real SAR stop fills intrabar at the stop price, not at the close. (4) No backtest and no costs (README l.19); one stock, two years, in-sample. (5) Fragile: initial values are set by chained assignment (l.46-50), which does nothing on pandas 3. new['date'] (l.156) does not match the 'Date' column the Heikin-Ashi script uses (l.188). It deletes 'Adj Close' (l.146), which newer yfinance versions may not return.
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: No PSAR was run in our repo. A close equivalent was: SIG-4, a Donchian channel ensemble with a ratcheting mid-line trailing exit, FAILED: B POST d +0.008 / w -0.049, C FULL d -0.365 / w -0.397 (resource/08 l.217; spec phase1_plan.md l.170; verdicts.md l.192-204). SIG-11, the breakout blend, also FAILED: breakout alone was below the sign rule, A FULL d -0.172 (resource/08 l.221). On stops: own-account day stops cost 0.07-0.13 Sharpe (resource/07 l.186; backtest_results.md l.242), and 'stops reshape drawdown, not edge' (resource/08 l.158). On speed: faster lookbacks scored worse (backtest_results.md l.237). Rejected-table row: resource/07 l.198.
strategies.fits_delta: An acceleration factor of 0.02-0.2 on daily bars is a fast system. Purely as mechanics, on synthetic random walks it reversed about once every 7-10 bars (test C); that says nothing about crypto edge. On fat-tailed 24/7 crypto it would flip often and pay 14.62 bps per round trip. A true stop-and-reverse also needs resting stop orders, which is a taker path. The MM bot's post-only rule forbids that (prev-week-levels memo l.33 and its 'What the code actually does' section make the same point for stop entries). It also needs highs and lows that the Delta close-only loader lacks (resource/08 l.95).
strategies.reason: This is a close equivalent rather than the same rule. A trailing-exit trend system at a speed faster than our rule is what SIG-4 (Donchian ratchet), SIG-11 (breakout) and T3d/T3i (faster lookbacks, stops) already tested and rejected. On top of that, the repo's SAR is not Wilder's SAR, and the script has no PnL code.

review.notes:
Bottom line: none of the four scripts is useful to us as a strategy or as tooling. They are 2018 indicator demos. Each runs on one US stock (BA, an unnamed ticker, NVDA, EA). README l.19 states the 'frictionless' assumption: no costs, no slippage. Three of the four have no PnL code at all. The one script with stats (Heikin-Ashi) evaluates at most 51 bars, because the portfolio runs on the plotting slice, and its omega and sortino ratios do not measure the strategy's returns.

Three things I found by re-typing their logic in my own code and running it on synthetic data (none of their code was executed or imported):
- The Awesome Oscillator 'saucer' never changes a trade, so that script is a plain SMA5/SMA34 crossover on the median price.
- The Parabolic SAR recursion is not Wilder's: after a reversal it builds on the old trend's value. It reversed 5,437 times against 4,025 for a textbook SAR, and its position differed on 11.0 % of bars.
- Chained assignment is used in every script. On pandas 3.0.5 it is a silent no-op, so the MACD script plots zero trades on current pandas.

Families against our evidence:
- Moving-average crossover (MACD, and AO in effect): tested and failed as SIG-3a, SIG-3b and T3d; SIG-6 was dropped (resource/08 l.83, l.120, l.215-216).
- Trailing-stop trend (Parabolic SAR): close equivalents SIG-4, SIG-11 and T3i failed (resource/08 l.217, l.221; resource/07 l.186).
- Heikin-Ashi entry: in effect a short-horizon dip-buy, which our evidence argues against (resource/07 l.175, l.201, l.205; crypto_academic.md l.52-53).

Screens list is empty because no family is both untested and plausible at our costs.

Evidence files (scratch, outside the repo):

strategies.name: London Breakout (London Breakout backtest.py; README.md lines 130-144)
strategies.what_it_does: An FX session-handoff opening-range breakout on one currency pair. Data: GBPUSD 1-minute bid/ask mid from histdata in New York time (data/gbpusd.csv: 29,698 rows, 2018-06-01 00:00 to 2018-06-29 16:58). Signal: upper/lower thresholds are the max/min of every minute price in the 02:00-02:59 EST hour (called 'tokyo_price', lines 112-113, 124-132). Entry: in the first 30 minutes after 03:00 EST (open_minutes=30, line 91; window lines 140-185) it goes long on the first minute whose price is above upper and short on the first below lower. It skips the entry if price is already more than risky_stop=0.01 beyond the threshold (line 84, lines 160, 178). Exit: a symmetric +/-0.005 target/stop from the entry price (lines 201-209), or a forced flat during hour 12 EST (lines 191-193). Sizing: one unit, +1/-1/0, no position sizing. Sample shown: main() builds signals for the whole month but plots only the first day (lines 277-280). The README shows two charts (preview/london breakout positions.png, thresholds.png). There are no PnL, Sharpe or trade statistics anywhere: line 282 points to the Heikin-Ashi script 'for stats'.
strategies.code_flaws: (1) No costs, spread or slippage. README.md:19 says outright 'all trades are frictionless. No slippage, no surcharge, no illiquidity', and fills are at the 1-minute mid of the bar that crossed the threshold. That is a same-bar touch fill with no queue, spread or stop-entry slippage. (2) No performance is computed at all. The 'backtest' is a signal plot of one day of one pair in one month, so there is no result to trust or reject. (3) Bug: plot() uses an undefined name 'signals' at line 245 (news=signals[f:l]). 'signals' is local to main(), so running the script as written should raise NameError, unless it runs in a notebook with a global of that name. Line 278 (new=new['%s'%date]) also uses DataFrame row indexing by date string through [], which newer pandas no longer supports. (4) Units are mislabelled. risky_stop=0.01 is called '100 basis points' (lines 75-84), but on GBPUSD at 1.326 it is 100 pips, about 75 bps (computed 0.01/1.326 = 0.754%). The target/stop of 0.005 is about 38 bps. The thresholds are absolute price, so they would not transfer across assets. (5) The target/stop is not checked during the 03:00-03:29 entry window (that elif branch holds only entry logic), so a position can blow through its stop for up to 30 minutes. (6) DST is ignored ('daylight saving time is another story', line 42). The only sample month, June 2018, is in BST/EDT. If histdata stamps are fixed UTC-5, as the script's comment at lines 38-41 says, then the coded 03:00 'London open' is 08:00 UTC, an hour after the real 07:00 UTC BST open. That last point is my inference from the comment. (7) O(n^2): cumsum is recomputed over the whole frame on most rows (lines 158, 176, 192, 202). (8) Parameters are hand-set and never varied or validated: 30 minutes, 0.01, 0.005, hour 2. One pair, one month, in-sample only. Survivorship is not relevant, since it is one FX pair.
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: No direct test of a session or fixed-hour opening-range breakout exists in our repo. The family evidence: (a) Intraday seasonality / session effects are on the rejected list. resource/07-trend-rule-and-prop-trading-research.md:178 says 'No consistent or persistent patterns' across seven exchanges and that a 1-2 hour window must beat ~10.6 bps plus spread every day; that row is literature only, [UNVERIFIED], with no backtest. Its research notes are cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-13-prop-strategy-evidence/designs/D3.md:185 and research_notes/.../academic_factor_evidence.md:133-140. (b) The repo's ORB literature review finds that 'Intraday breakout and ORB evidence is mostly gross, and tends to vanish net of spread and slippage' (Zarattini & Aziz vs its MQL5 replication; Neely & Weller; Curcio et al.). See cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-22-prev-week-levels-evidence/literature/literature.md:120-130 and :266. (c) The closest tested trade, a stop entry at a prior-range extreme held for hours, is the previous-week touch-breakout. It made only +7.8 bps/trade net at base taker costs on 15 unseen perps 2022-26 (P 0.25) and -8.2 bps at stress costs, and it lost in 2023 and 2024. The confirmed 1 h breakout lost on 25 coins (-10.8 net) and on Delta (-51.1 net). Sources: cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-22-prev-week-levels.md:31-35, :42, :45, and the rejected-table row at resource/07-trend-rule-and-prop-trading-research.md:205. (d) What the repo does know about crypto time of day is about activity and volatility, not direction: ~2,000 fills/day-equivalent in the IST evening vs ~790 overnight (cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-09-30-shadow-dism-ada-avax.md:21), and an hour-of-day spread-multiplier idea for the MM (resource/02-practitioner-articles.md:342-347).
strategies.fits_delta: Poor. The premise is that London FX liquidity dominates the Tokyo-to-London handoff (README.md:134-136). That has no counterpart on Delta perps, which trade 24/7 with no session open, no overnight gap and no 'closed foreign market' to peek at. A crypto port would have to pick an arbitrary UTC hour (Asia 00:00, US cash open 13:30). That is choosing the hour for performance, which the repo already treats as a curve-fit risk (resource/07:178 seasonality row; the D2 decision-hour row at resource/07:199). Execution: a breakout entry is a stop/taker order, and so is a stop/target exit, so a round trip costs 14.62 bps at base (prev-week memo line 33). The post-only MM bot cannot carry it: .claude/rules/cex-mm.md:24 says 'Quoting orders are post-only. The only taker path is reduce-only for a hard-cap or risk exit', and the prev-week memo line 52 says the same. The script's own 38 bps target sits against a 14.62 bps cost, and a 75 bps stop is about 2.6x that target. The closest crypto analog with a real stop-cluster mechanism (weekly extremes) moved only about 20-30 bps in 4 h gross (prev-week memo line 32). A one-hour pre-session range is a much less salient level.
strategies.reason: It is an FX-session-specific idea shown as a one-day, one-pair, frictionless signal plot with no PnL computed and a NameError in its plot function. Its crypto translation, a fixed-hour range breakout, is an intraday ORB. The repo's literature review finds ORB edges vanish net of costs (literature.md:266). The repo rejected intraday seasonality (resource/07:178). Its closest tested cousin, the prior-range touch-breakout, did not clear 14.62 bps round trip on recent unseen perps (prev-week memo lines 34-35, 45). It also needs a taker order path the bot forbids. Nothing in the code is worth reusing.

strategies.name: Dual Thrust (Dual Thrust backtest.py; README.md lines 174-184)
strategies.what_it_does: An intraday open-plus-range breakout, stop-and-reverse, on the same GBPUSD 1-minute mid file (June 2018). Daily bars come from the 03:00-12:00 EST window only (min2day, lines 43-79). This uses only the first month in the file (year/month from df.index[0], lines 222-226). Range = max(HH - LC, HC - LL) over rg=5 daily bars (lines 83-85; rg=5, param=0.5 at lines 218-219). Thresholds are set at the 03:00 EST bar: sigup = price_03:00 + 0.5*Range and siglo = price_03:00 - 0.5*Range (lines 127-129). Entry: long when the minute price is above sigup, short when below siglo; only one unit is held (cumsum guard, lines 141-144). It reverses (signal +/-2) if price later crosses the opposite threshold (lines 148-152). There is no stop or target (README.md:178). Exit: all positions close at 12:00 EST (lines 157-160). Sizing: one unit. As in London Breakout, nothing is computed beyond signals: the plot shows one hand-picked day ('i go to -3 is that day we execute a trade', lines 172-175). Stats are deferred to Heikin-Ashi (line 230). The rule follows the QuantConnect tutorial cited at line 18.
strategies.code_flaws: (1) Look-ahead, and it is decisive. intraday['range'][date] (lines 128-129) is read at 03:00 of day d. It is a rolling(5) window whose last row is day d itself (lines 83-85), and day d's high, low and close come from 03:00-12:00 of that same day. So the thresholds set at the open already contain that day's high, low and 12:00 close. Correct Dual Thrust uses the previous N days (Range should be shifted by one day). This contaminates every trade it would generate. (2) No costs, spread or slippage (README.md:19). Fills are at the 1-minute mid of the crossing bar, with no stop-entry slippage. A reversal trades 2 units with zero cost. (3) No performance computed. One plotted day, explicitly chosen because it has a trade (lines 172-175). Effectively one month of one pair, in-sample, with parameters fixed at 0.5/5 and never varied. (4) Bug at the 12:00 bar. Thresholds are still live on that bar, so a reversal can fire first (signal -2 against a +1 position). Line 159 then recomputes cumsum to -1 and line 160 sets the bar's signal to +1, which leaves the position at +2 instead of flat. strategies.reason: The script's backtest is invalid as written: the thresholds use the same day's high, low and close (look-ahead), there are no costs, and it shows one cherry-picked day with no PnL. strategies.name: Bollinger Bands bottom-W pattern recognition (Bollinger Bands Pattern Recognition backtest.py; README section 9, lines 198-212)
strategies.what_it_does: Bands: 20-bar rolling mean of price ±2 rolling std (lines 39-47). Long-only 'bottom W' entry at bar i (lines 93-152): (cond 4) price[i] > upper band[i] and flat; scanning back up to period=75 bars: (cond 2) a bar j where |mid[j]-price[j]| < alpha AND |mid[j]-upper[i]| < alpha; (cond 1) a bar k <= j where |lower[k]-price[k]| < alpha (first bottom, threshold = price[k]); a bar l with price above mid (used only for the drawing); (cond 3) a bar m between j and i with 0 < price[m]-lower[m] < alpha and price[m] < threshold (the second, lower bottom). alpha = beta = 0.0001 in absolute price units (lines 81-82). Exit (lines 163-167): close the long when rolling std < beta (band contraction). Fixed one-unit position, no stop and no time stop, top-M short not implemented. Shown on one month of GBPUSD 1-minute mid prices from histdata (data/gbpusd.csv: 29,698 rows, 2018-06-01 00:00 to 2018-06-29 16:58; main() line 225). review.notes:
Bottom line: none of the three scripts is useful to us. None computes PnL or costs (README line 19: 'all trades are frictionless'), each is a single-asset in-sample picture (GBPUSD 1-min June 2018, FCAU daily 2016-17, VOD.L daily 2000-21 with a 16-bar display window), and two have hard look-ahead (Shooting Star conditions 7-8 use the next bar; condition 3 uses a full-sample mean). Under pandas 3 (3.0.5 here) all three break or silently change behaviour. I checked each pattern in my own toy code, never by running theirs: chained assignment never writes, so RSI stays 0 and that script is always long; integer lookups on a DatetimeIndex raise KeyError; the Bollinger date format raises ValueError. The RSI 'head-and-shoulders on RSI' is actually detected on Close prices and is never called by main().

What I computed, all re-implemented from scratch with nothing imported from the external repo:
- Data and settings: Binance USDT-M daily candles for our nine coins from the existing cache (scratchpad/trend-cache), 2020-05-01..2026-09-30. Signal at close t, held t to t+1, 7.31 bps per side (14.62 round trip), no funding. Descriptive and not pre-registered: one run per rule, no multiple-testing haircut.
- RSI14 30/70 long/short: net Sharpe -0.72 (2022-26: -0.47).
- BB20/2 revert-to-mid long/short: -0.44 (2022-26: -0.21).
- The long-only legs only match the always-long basket (2022-26: RSI<30 0.42, BB 0.24, basket 0.38). The BB leg has no timing content: held-day 20.6 bps vs 20.7 bps unconditional.
- RSI<30 long, 2022-26: date-clustered t 0.30, excess over the basket -17.3 bps (t -1.88), and five months carry all of its profit.
- Shooting star fires 0 times on 24/7 bars.

strategies.code_flaws: (1) The thresholds mix units. The bands are z_onset +/- np.std(model.resid), where z has no units and the residual sd is in AMD dollars, and they are centred on z at onset, not on 0 (lines 162-163). This contradicts the README's +/-1 sigma. (2) The exit is at band re-entry, not at the mean, so a winning trade earns only the small crossing amount. Holding while the spread diverges has no stop. (3) The signal is computed on bar t's close and filled at that same close. (4) Each leg's share count uses max(price) over the full sample, which is look-ahead (lines 252-253). The legs are not sized by the hedge ratio, so the spread is not actually hedged. (5) The ADF p-value uses Dickey-Fuller tables on an estimated residual (line 77). Engle-Granger needs MacKinnon cointegration values, so the test over-accepts. It is re-run every bar at 5%, a multiple-testing problem. (6) A model frozen at onset is used for trading while the test is refit daily (lines 130-157). (7) No costs, no borrow or funding. (8) One hand-picked pair, about 1 year traded after warm-up, in sample. (9) The chained assignments signals['z'].iloc[i:]=... (lines 139-163) are silent no-ops under pandas 3. I copied the pattern into my own script on pandas 3.0.5: the column stayed NaN with a ChainedAssignmentError. So z stays NaN, no trade ever fires, and main()'s dropna().index[0] (line 332) would fail. Quick check, with the bugs fixed and re-implemented in my own code on the nine's 36 pairs (log prices, next-day hold, 7.31 bps/side, funding charged): net Sharpe -0.42 FULL 2020-05..2026-09, -0.87 for 2020-21, -0.21 for 2022-26, -0.36 for 2024-26; 1,131 round trips; mean gross -29.2 bps per trip (median +120.4) against about 29.2 bps of cost. A fat left tail from spreads that never come back makes the mean negative.
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: Literature only, never backtested. Grepping the repo for cointegr/adfuller/hedge_ratio finds only notes. cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-13-prop-strategy-evidence/research_notes/Crypto strategy for prop trading/practitioner_strategies.md lines 107-134 (KQ4). Line 118: in a Utupub thesis covering 2020-22, daily cointegration was 'the only profitable strategy after transaction costs' while all hourly methods lost. Line 128 infers that daily cointegration pairs on large coins is the only stat-arb variant with a net-of-cost positive result. Neighbouring families that were rejected: resource/07-trend-rule-and-prop-trading-research.md line 179 (cross-sectional alt momentum / beta-neutral baskets, rejected on literature and a GitHub README) and line 180 (BTC->alt lead-lag works only at seconds scale). Shorts in the trend rule were rejected on our own backtest (07 line 183), and 07 line 237 bars shorts and a second strategy for the current program. resource/08 line 172: the nine are 1.50 effective bets, with correlation near 0.75 in bear years. practitioner_strategies.md line 100: short-alts vs long-BTC was directionally right since late 2024, so alt/BTC spreads have trended.
strategies.fits_delta: It partly fits. Delta lists all nine as perps and shorting is native. The book trades at daily frequency, so 4 taker fills per pair round trip, 4 x 7.31 = 29.24 bps of leg notional, is small next to typical spread excursions (median gross per trip in the quick check +120 bps). Funding applies to both legs: the short leg receives positive funding and the long leg pays it (08 line 181 lists realized Delta funding by coin). It is a taker book separate from the post-only MM, so it does not touch the post-only invariant. Concerns: the spreads are non-stationary (alt/BTC downtrends), the 07 line 237 policy conflict, and whole-contract rounding on two legs at $1,000.
strategies.reason: The repo's own script is unusable: its band arithmetic is broken, it exits at the band, it has no costs, and it no-ops under pandas 3. The faithful fixed rule loses on our nine (Sharpe -0.42). The family, though, is genuinely untested by any backtest in our repo, and the one literature note we hold says daily cointegration is the variant that survived costs. A properly specified rule with a half-life filter, exit near the mean, a divergence stop and a time stop is worth one pre-registered screen (PAIR-1, frozen before any pairs computation).

strategies.name: Oil Money momentum rule, 'Oil Money project/Oil Money Trading backtest.py' (NOKJPY vs Brent; COPAUD vs Vasconia)
strategies.what_it_does: When flat and untrained, it fits OLS of NOKJPY on Brent-in-JPY over the last 50 closes. If R^2 > 0.7, it freezes that model and a +/-2 sigma residual band (lines 117-147). The model is not refit until a trade closes. When NOK closes above fitted + 2 sigma it goes long; below fitted - 2 sigma it goes short. This follows the break; it does not fade it (lines 151-175). Exits: the position closes when the counter exceeds 10 bars (12 bars held), or when |price - entry| >= 0.5 points (0.001 for COP) (lines 85-109). Sizing is capital0 // max(close) (line 189). Only the currency leg is traded. Data: NOKJPY 2013-04-25..2018-04-24 (1,289 rows); COPAUD 2014-01-02..2019-01-01, traded from 2016 (COP.py line 291). The rule came out of a failed fade strategy, NOK.py lines 245-270: fade at 1 sigma, flip at 2 sigma, with the model fit before 2017-04-25. After the 2017-11-15 break the author noticed momentum (README lines 71-91) and then wrote this rule (README lines 95-99).
strategies.code_flaws: (1) It was discovered after one event (the NOK break of 2017-11-15) and backtested on the same data, so it is in sample. (2) The holding period and stop were picked from grids: 15 x 16 = 240 combinations for NOK (NOK.py lines 479-486) and 15 x 8 = 120 for COP (COP.py lines 315-322). The author picked the best cell: 'optimal' 9 days for NOK (README line 111), and '17 days ... maximum return, 9%' for COP (README line 284). The grid means were about 2% for NOK (README line 107) and 7% for COP (README line 280). (3) The signal and the fill use the same close (lines 152-154 with portfolio lines 194-198). (4) Sizing uses the full-sample max price (line 189). (5) Stops are in absolute price points, so they depend on the price scale. (6) No costs (README line 19). (7) The README claims 'market neutrality' (README line 290), but only the currency is held (lines 187-198). (8) A trained model persists while flat, so signals come from stale fits. (9) The analysis scripts do not run as published. NOK.py has a string literal broken across lines 132-133, an undefined `dataset` at line 466, a missing comma at line 481, and imports a module name (line 462) that does not match the file name. os.chdir('d:/') is hard-coded (backtest line 16). (10) In the CAD and COP 'out-of-sample' regressions the OLS is fit on the test half (CAD.py line 348; COP.py lines 220 and 258). So the README's claim that out-of-sample beats in-sample (README lines 203, 270) is an artifact. (11) The CAD regime split comes from K-Means on the full sample with the date as a feature (CAD.py lines 208-265), which is hindsight. Two currencies 'work' only after RUB and CAD were discarded (README lines 159, 208), which is selection.
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: The unhedged single-leg crypto analogue (an alt breaking out of its BTC-implied value, then followed) is a breakout and relative-strength rule. Close equivalents: Donchian ratchet SIG-4 and the breakout blend SIG-11 both FAIL (resource/08 lines 217, 221). Previous-week-level breakouts fail after Delta costs (cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-22-prev-week-levels.md line 25). Relative strength vs BTC: OVL-7 was dropped as 'relative strength in disguise' (cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-22-trend-improvement-evidence/phase1/master_candidates.md line 462; phase1_plan.md line 407). Cross-sectional alt momentum and beta-neutral baskets were rejected, but on literature only (07 line 179). The shorts in the trend rule were rejected on our own backtest (07 line 183). Residual momentum appears only as a literature note (phase1/notes/crypto_academic.md line 129). No BTC-hedged time-series version of residual-break momentum has been backtested. Quick check on the nine (repo parameters, ln prices, next-day hold, 7.31 bps/side, funding). Unhedged L/S, as in the repo: Sharpe 0.44 FULL, -0.33 for 2020-21, 0.79 for 2022-26, max DD -46.4%, 412 entries; the short leg lost 59.8% (sum of daily returns) in 2021. The same entries hedged with beta x BTC: Sharpe 0.89 FULL and 0.54 for 2022-26, by year +33.5/+31.6/+19.0/+25.0/-12.6/+25.0/-18.1%. Mean net per trade +225.4 bps, median +83.8, 53.4% positive.
strategies.fits_delta: The petrocurrency version does not fit: Delta has no FX or crude perps. The transplant (alt vs BTC on Delta perps) fits mechanically. The trade lasts about 12 days and gross per trade is far above the 29.24 bps hedged round trip, and the BTC hedge leg is cheap at a 0.06 bps touch. But it needs shorts (BTC hedge or alt short), which 07 line 237 bars. It also overlaps the long/flat trend book on the long-alt side, so the correlation must be measured.
strategies.reason: As published (FX, single-leg, grid-optimised, same-close fills, scripts that do not run) it is not usable, and the unhedged form is the shorts and breakout family our repo already rejected. The BTC-hedged transplant, though, has never been backtested here. Its nearest rejected neighbour (07 line 179) was rejected on literature, not on our data. My one look with the repo's own parameters cleared costs by a wide margin. It goes as RESID-1, with the pass judged only on the 16 ex-ante perps this review never loaded.

The CAD/COP 'out-of-sample' fits are fit on the test data (CAD.py line 348; COP.py lines 220, 258), and the CAD regimes come from full-sample K-Means using the date as a feature (CAD.py lines 208-265). strategies.name: Monte Carlo project (GBM best-fit path as a forecaster)
strategies.what_it_does: It is a debunk, not a strategy. It simulates N GBM paths from the training-half log-return mean and sd, picks the path closest to realized training prices (minimum sd of the difference), and checks whether that path predicts the test-half direction and the tail. Tickers: GE 2016-01-15..2019-01-15 and NVDA 2006-2009, split 50/50 (MC README lines 9, 29-33; code lines 212-261, 322-346). Conclusion: accuracy is a coin toss regardless of 500-1,500 simulations (README line 23), and the lowest simulated price missed the real lows: 10.99 vs 6.71 for GE, 6.086 vs 5.9 for NVDA (README lines 29, 33).
strategies.code_flaws: (1) The drift subtracts var/2 from a mean that is already a log-return mean (line 225), so the paths are biased downward twice. (2) Gaussian shocks (line 242) make the 'fat-tail' test a test of a thin-tailed model, not of Monte Carlo itself. (3) Each simulation count is one random draw scored once, so the accuracy-versus-number-of-simulations chart is single Bernoulli trials. (4) Single stocks, one split each. The direction sign is computed as start minus end for both actual and forecast (lines 342-345), which is inverted but harmless. (5) It uses the deprecated fix_yahoo_finance.
strategies.prior_evidence_in_our_repo: Our repo already uses resampling for inference, not GBM path-picking: the week-cluster bootstrap with 2,000 draws in cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-22-prev-week-levels.md line 18, bootstrap pass and breach shares in resource/07 line 137, and bootstrap CIs and hurdles throughout resource/08 (e.g. line 233).
strategies.fits_delta: Not a trading idea. Its lesson, that a fitted random path has no predictive content and that normal shocks understate crypto tails, is consistent with what we already do.
strategies.reason: Its conclusion is correct and is already embodied in our bootstrap-based methodology. There is nothing to adopt or test.

screens.rule: Daily cointegration spread reversion, market-neutral pairs. Universe: all 36 pairs of the nine Delta perps (BTC ETH XRP BNB ADA LTC LINK DOGE BCH). Breadth panel: the 24 ex-ante Binance USDT-M perps listed by 2020-02-20, 276 pairs, 2022-01..2026-09. Venue check: Delta daily closes and funding on the nine, 2024-08..2026-10. Data: Binance USDT-M 1d klines (00:00 UTC close), 1h klines for fills, 8h funding. Legs: X is the coin earlier in [BTC, ETH, XRP, BNB, ADA, LTC, LINK, DOGE, BCH] (24-panel: by 30-day median turnover at 2020-02-20) and Y is the later one. Formation every Monday 00:00 UTC, on data up to that close only: OLS ln P_Y = a + b ln P_X over the trailing 180 daily closes. A pair is eligible if the Engle-Granger p-value is < 0.05 (MacKinnon cointegration values, constant, AIC lag choice up to 10), b is in [0.25, 4], and the OU half-life h = -ln2/ln(1+c) from de_t = k + c e_{t-1} (c < 0) is in [2, 30] days. Keep up to K = 4 pairs by lowest p, with each coin in at most 2 pairs. Signal at the daily close: z_t = (ln P_Y - b ln P_X - a - mean_e)/sd_e, with all parameters frozen at formation. Entry when flat and the pair is selected: z >= +2 means short Y and long b*N of X; z <= -2 is the reverse. Fill at the 01:00 UTC hourly close, never the decision bar. Sizing: Y notional N, X notional b*N, with N set so the ex-ante spread vol is 0.10/sqrt(K) a year; per-pair gross <= 0.5x equity and total gross <= 2.0x. Exit at the first of: |z| <= 0.5; |z| >= 4 (stop); days held > min(2h, 30); Monday re-test p > 0.20. An open pair keeps its entry parameters. No re-entry for 3 days after a stop. Costs: every leg fill 5.31 bps taker + 2 bps slippage = 7.31 bps/side/leg (29.24 bps per equal-legged pair round trip), with a 10 bps slippage stress. Funding is charged on both legs at every stamp. Daily mark-to-market. Pass, all required: net Sharpe >= 0.50 on the nine 2020-05..2026-09; > 0 in both 2020-05..2023-12 and 2024-01..2026-09; > 0 on the 24-panel 2022-26; mean net per round trip >= +29.24 bps of leg notional; week-cluster bootstrap (2,000) P(Sharpe <= 0) <= 0.10; Sharpe > 0 at 10 bps slippage; |corr| with the weekly TV 0.25 trend book <= 0.30. Labelled neighbours (window 120/365, entry 1.5/2.5, K 2/6) are reported but never selected. Spec frozen before any pairs computation: ext_repo/review/stat-arb-and-macro/screen_PAIR1_frozen.txt, sha256 5556a0cdcc03c5e4ae1df28bb3ad3d543decfbb82898f970595a4a28c8a70c06.
screens.why_untested: Our repo has only literature notes on cointegration pairs (practitioner_strategies.md lines 107-134; line 128 calls daily cointegration on large coins the only stat-arb variant net-positive after costs). There is no backtest in any memo, script or evidence folder. The rejected rows are different families: cross-sectional momentum and beta-neutral baskets on literature (07 line 179), seconds-scale lead-lag (07 line 180), and trend shorts (07 line 183). The repo's literal rule lost in my quick check (Sharpe -0.42). Its median trip still grossed +120 bps against 29 bps of cost, with losses coming from divergences that a stop, a half-life filter and a mean exit address. So surviving costs is plausible but unproven.

screens.rule: BTC-hedged 'co-movement break, follow it' (the Oil Money rule moved to alt vs BTC). Pass panel, which this review never loaded: the 16 ex-ante Binance USDT-M perps outside the nine, listed by 2020-02-20 (ATOM BAT DASH EOS ETC IOST IOTA NEO ONT QTUM TRX VET XLM XMR XTZ ZEC), 2020-05..2026-09, driver X = BTC. The nine's 8 alts on Binance 2020-26 and the Delta nine 2024-08..2026-10 are reported as reference only. Data: Binance 1d klines (00:00 UTC), 1h for fills, 8h funding. Rule per alt, in ln prices, following the logic of 'Oil Money Trading backtest.py' with state holding in {-1,0,+1}, trained and counter. Each day: if holding != 0, close when counter > 10 (holding = 0, trained = False, counter = 0) and skip the day; otherwise counter += 1. If flat and untrained: OLS ln Y = a + b ln BTC on closes [t-50, t-1]; if R^2 > 0.70, set trained and freeze a, b and sigma = sd of the window residual until the next trade closes. If trained: f = a + b ln BTC_t; ln Y_t > f + 2 sigma means holding = +1, and ln Y_t < f - 2 sigma means holding = -1. No price stop. Position: +1 is long Y notional N and short b*N BTC; -1 is the reverse, with the hedge fixed at entry and N = equity / number of alts. Fill at the 01:00 UTC hourly close after the decision. Costs: 5.31 bps taker + 2 bps slippage per leg fill (29.24 bps per equal-legged round trip), funding on both legs, and a 10 bps slippage stress. Pass, all on the 16 unseen perps: net Sharpe >= 0.50; > 0 in both 2020-05..2023-12 and 2024-01..2026-09; mean net per round trip >= +29.24 bps of alt notional; week-cluster bootstrap (2,000) P(Sharpe <= 0) <= 0.10; Sharpe > 0 at 10 bps slippage; |corr| with the weekly trend book run on the same 16 <= 0.30. Labelled neighbours, never selected: fill at the decision close; daily refit while flat; R^2 0.6/0.8; band 1.5/2.5 sigma; hold 6/18 bars; unhedged single leg. Spec frozen after one descriptive look on the nine with the repo's own parameters and no tuning: ext_repo/review/stat-arb-and-macro/screen_RESID1_frozen.txt, sha256 9f5a62a0efc4f6ddf5e97089f2b8fcc0e7de1479caec8293837003227afc8e60.

Its nearest neighbour, cross-sectional alt momentum and beta-neutral baskets, was rejected on literature and a GitHub README only (07 line 179). OVL-7 relative strength vs BTC was dropped without a backtest (master_candidates.md line 462; phase1_plan.md line 407). Residual momentum exists only as a literature note (crypto_academic.md line 129). The unhedged single-leg form overlaps rejected breakouts (08 lines 217, 221) and rejected shorts (07 line 183), which is why only the hedged form is proposed. But 2024 (-12.6%) and 2026 YTD (-18.1%) were negative, and those numbers are on seen data, hence the unseen-panel pass rule.

Quick check: descriptive, one run per rule, not pre-registered, no multiple-testing haircut. Costs were 7.31 bps per side, funding was charged, and each position was held from close t to close t+1.
- **Pair rule, bugs fixed, 36 pairs:** net Sharpe -0.42 over 2020-05..2026-09, max drawdown -11.9%. Per round trip the mean gross was -29.2 bps and the median +120.4 bps, against about 29.2 bps of cost.
- **Oil Money rule on alt vs BTC, unhedged long/short (the repo's form):** Sharpe 0.44 full period, -0.33 in 2020-21, 0.79 in 2022-26. Max drawdown -46.4%. The short leg lost 59.8% (sum of daily returns) in 2021.

- **Reference:** equal-weight always-long nine, no cost, Sharpe 1.01.

Caveats on the two screens:
- PAIR-1 was frozen before any pairs computation on crypto data.
- RESID-1 was frozen after one look. It keeps the repo's own parameters, but the nine have now been seen, so its pass is judged only on the 16 unseen ex-ante perps.
- Both need short legs. resource/07 line 237 bars shorts and a second strategy in the current program, so a pass only reopens the question for the user. Nothing changes in the running books.

screens.rule: Research only, on public Delta data; no orders. Universe: Delta India BTC and ETH European options (XAUT is excluded: only 2 expiries listed).
